_doc: Every word of Moments, the family Story and the Odd Sheet. One row per kind of beat, or per story id. Each list is variants; the same beat always gets the same variant, picked by its number. head = a newspaper headline, line = a plain sentence for a Moment or a family's story, body = the paper's first paragraph. {who} {person} {other} {a} {b} = first names, {full} = whole name, {place} {cause} {rooms} {amount} {seconds}. Plain words, no real brands, no other game's names.

line: Fire at {place}. The engine is on its way.
Smoke over {place}. The crew are rolling.
head: FIRE AT {PLACE}
{PLACE} ALIGHT
body: Crews were called to {place}, where {cause} is blamed.

line: {who} is trapped inside {place}.
{who} can't get out of {place}.
head: {WHO} TRAPPED AT {PLACE}
body: {who} was cut off inside {place} as the smoke came down.

line: {who} carried {person} out of {place}.
{person} is out of {place}, over {who}'s shoulder.
head: {WHO} CARRIES {PERSON} TO SAFETY
HERO OF {PLACE}: {WHO}
"I JUST PICKED THEM UP," SAYS {WHO}
body: {who} went into the smoke at {place} and came out with {person} over one shoulder. {person} has promised to buy the drinks for a year.
Bystanders at {place} watched {who} carry {person} out of the front door. {who} would not be drawn on the subject of the wig.

line: The fire at {place} is out. {roomcount} damaged.
Fire out at {place}, {roomcount} burned. It was {cause}, they say.
head: {PLACE} GUTTED
FIRE TAKES {rooms} ROOMS AT {PLACE}
{CAUSE} BLAMED FOR {PLACE} BLAZE
body: {cause} started it. {roomcount} of {place} are burned, and {seconds} seconds of hard work put it out. The insurers have been told.
It took the crew {seconds} seconds to put out the fire at {place}. The cause, they say, was {cause}. Boards are on order.

line: {who} has gone to the clinic from {place}.
head: {WHO} TAKEN TO CLINIC
body: {who} was taken from {place} by ambulance, coughing, and asking who was feeding the cat.

line: {who} is out of the clinic and home.
head: {WHO} HOME FROM CLINIC
body: {who} walked out of the clinic today. The nurses say they will miss the complaints.

line: The family have moved out of {place} until the repairs are done.
Burned out of {place}. The county has found them somewhere to stay.
head: FAMILY MOVED OUT OF {PLACE}
body: The household at {place} is sleeping somewhere else tonight. The county is covering it.

line: Home again: the repairs are done at {place} and they have moved back.
head: BACK HOME AT LAST
body: The family from {place} have moved back in. It smells of new wood.

line: The repairs are done at {place}, with {boards} boards from the yard.
head: {PLACE} REBUILT
body: {place} is back, with {boards} new boards from Wend Mill.

line: {who} got a promotion.
head: {WHO} MOVES UP IN THE WORLD
body: {who} has been promoted. The office cake was, by all accounts, adequate.

line: {a} and {b} are friends now.
head: {A} AND {B}: IT'S OFFICIAL
body: {a} and {b} are now to be seen together. Nobody saw it coming.

line: {a} and {b} had words.
head: WORDS EXCHANGED
body: {a} and {b} had words. Witnesses report that some of the words were long.

line: {a} and {b} made a scene.
head: A SCENE
body: {a} and {b} made a scene in public, and the town would like to know more.

line: The county had to step in with a grant.
head: COUNTY PAYS UP
body: A household was helped out by the county. This should not happen.

line: {who}'s car ended up on its roof. The tow gnome came.
head: GNOME RIGHTS CAR
body: {who}'s car was found upside down. The tow gnome declined to comment, and sent a bill.

line: {who} had a small mishap at work.
head: PLASTER APPLIED
body: {who} had a mishap at work. A plaster was involved.

line: {who} has a new job.
head: {WHO} STARTS MONDAY
body: {who} has taken a new job, and has been told not to be late.

line: It was {who}'s birthday.
{who} turned {age}. There was cake.
head: MANY HAPPY RETURNS, {WHO}
body: {who} is {age} today, and has asked us not to mention it.

line: {who} found {amount} coins on the pavement.
head: PAVEMENT PAYS OUT
body: {who} found {amount} coins on the pavement and has told everybody.

line: {who} and {other} fell out over the fence.
{who} told {other} exactly what they think of the hedge.
head: THE WAR OF THE HEDGE
body: {who} and {other} are no longer speaking. It is about the hedge, as it always is.

line: {other} brought {who} a plant.
{who} helped {other} carry the shopping in.
head: GOOD NEIGHBOURS
body: {who} and {other} were seen being nice to each other. We will keep an eye on it.

line: {who} went on a date with {other}.
{who} met {other} for a coffee that lasted four hours.
head: SEEN TOGETHER: {WHO} AND {OTHER}
body: {who} and {other} were seen sharing a table. Sources say there was laughing.

line: {who} and {other} went out again.
{who} is seeing {other} again. The family have noticed.
head: {WHO} AND {OTHER}, AGAIN
body: That is twice now for {who} and {other}. The town has started a sweepstake.

line: {who} and {other} are a couple now.
head: IT'S LOVE: {WHO} AND {OTHER}
body: {who} and {other} have told their families. The sweepstake has paid out.

line: {who} lost the keys. They were in the fridge.
head: KEYS FOUND IN FRIDGE
body: {who} spent the morning looking for the keys. They were in the fridge.

line: {who}'s car made a noise. {amount} coins later, it stopped.
head: THAT NOISE
body: {who} paid to have a noise taken out of the car.

line: {who} has a cold and wants everybody to know.
head: COLD GOING ROUND
body: {who} has a cold. Please stand well back.

line: {who} won the pub quiz: {amount} coins.
head: {WHO} KNOWS THE CAPITAL OF EVERYWHERE
body: {who} won the pub quiz and {amount} coins. There has been a complaint.

line: A small spell of {who}'s went wrong. The kettle is now a very small horse.
{who} tried a small spell. Their eyebrows are blue.
head: SPELL GOES SLIGHTLY WRONG
body: {who} attempted a small spell at home. The results are still in the kitchen.

line: A duck followed {who} all the way to the shops.
{who} has been adopted by a duck.
head: DUCK FOLLOWS RESIDENT
body: A duck has been following {who} around town. Neither party will explain.

line: {other} brought {who} a pie after the fire.
head: THE STREET LOOKS AFTER ITS OWN
body: {other} turned up at the door with a pie for {who}. It helped.

line: {who} asked {other} out.
{who} has asked {other} for a coffee. Nobody is calling it a date. It is a date.
head: {WHO} HAS ASKED {OTHER} OUT
body: {who} has asked {other} out, in a voice witnesses describe as "quite high". They are to meet at {place}.

line: {who} and {other} had a first date at {place}. It went well.
Four hours at {place} for {who} and {other}. They forgot to order.
head: SEEN TOGETHER: {WHO} AND {OTHER}
FIRST DATE, NO CASUALTIES
body: {who} and {other} shared a table at {place}. Sources say there was laughing, and that it was not nervous by the end.

line: {who} and {other} had a first date at {place}. There will not be a second.
{other} left the date with {who} early, by the kitchen.
head: DATE ENDS IN SILENCE AT {PLACE}
body: {who} and {other} tried a date at {place}. Staff report one of the longest silences in the history of the building.

line: {who} waited at {place}. {other} never came.
{other} stood {who} up at {place}.
head: STOOD UP AT {PLACE}
body: {who} sat alone at {place} for most of an hour, and has been heard asking what {other} thinks they are playing at.

line: {who} and {other} went out again, and it went better.
That is twice now for {who} and {other}.
head: {WHO} AND {OTHER}, AGAIN
body: That is twice now for {who} and {other}. The town has started a sweepstake.

line: The second date did not go like the first: {who} and {other} left separately.
head: THE SECOND DATE: NOT A SUCCESS
body: Whatever {who} and {other} had at the first date, they did not bring it to the second.

line: {who} and {other} are a couple now.
head: IT'S LOVE: {WHO} AND {OTHER}
body: {who} and {other} have told their families. The sweepstake has paid out.

line: {who} met {other}'s family. Everyone was very polite. It was awful.
head: {WHO} MEETS THE FAMILY
body: {who} has been to dinner with {other}'s family, and answered all the questions.

line: {who} and {other} are seeing each other, and their families are not speaking.
Two houses at war over {cause}, and {who} and {other} have gone on a date.
head: LOVE ACROSS THE FENCE
body: With their families still at war over {cause}, {who} and {other} have been making plans. This column has bought popcorn.

line: {who} asked {other} at {place}. {other} said yes!
head: {WHO} ASKS, {OTHER} SAYS YES
body: {who} got down on one knee at {place}, and needed some help getting back up. The answer was yes.

line: {who} asked {other} at {place}. {other} said not yet.
head: "NOT YET," SAYS {OTHER}
body: {who} asked the question at {place}. The answer was "not yet", which {who} is trying to find encouraging.

line: {who} and {other} got married at {place}, with {guests} guests.
head: {WHO} AND {OTHER}: MARRIED
THE TOWN TURNS OUT FOR {WHO} AND {OTHER}
body: {who} and {other} were married at {place} in front of {guests} guests, several of whom had money on it.

line: {who} and {other} have moved in together.
head: ONE HOME, TWO TOOTHBRUSHES
body: {who} and {other} have set up home. Decisions about the sofa are ongoing.

line: {who} and {other} have called it off.
head: IT'S OVER FOR {WHO} AND {OTHER}
body: {who} and {other} are no longer an item. The sweepstake organisers have declined to comment.

line: {who} and {other} have fallen out over {cause}.
It started with {cause}. {who} and {other} are not speaking.
head: TROUBLE BREWING: {WHO} AND {OTHER}
body: {who} and {other} have fallen out over {cause}. Neighbours expect this to run.

line: {who} told {other} what they think about {cause}. At length.
{who} and {other} had words about {cause} again.
head: WORDS OVER {CAUSE}
body: {who} and {other} were heard discussing {cause} at a volume that discouraged anyone from joining in.

line: {who} {prank}. {other} knows exactly who did it.
{other} woke to find {who} had {prank2}.
head: THE WAR GOES ON: {WHO} STRIKES
body: The business of {cause} goes on. {who} {prank}, and {other} has put a sign up.

line: {who} and {other} had it out at {place}, in front of everyone.
A public row at {place}: {who} against {other}, over {cause}.
head: SCENES AT {PLACE}
{WHO} AND {OTHER} GO PUBLIC
body: The matter of {cause} boiled over at {place}, where {who} and {other} had an audience and used it.

line: The town hall has ruled: {who} is in the right about {cause}. {other} paid {amount} coins.
{who} won the hearing over {cause}. {other} says it is not over. It is over.
head: TOWN HALL RULES FOR {WHO}
body: After a hearing about {cause}, the town clerk found for {who} and fined {other} {amount} coins. The clerk has asked never to hear the word again.

line: {other} did not turn up to the hearing about {cause}. {who} says that says it all.
head: EMPTY CHAIR AT THE HEARING
body: The hearing into {cause} lasted four minutes, because only {who} came.

line: {who} and {other} have made it up. Nobody mentioned {cause}.
It's over: {who} took a casserole round to {other}.
head: PEACE BREAKS OUT: {WHO} AND {OTHER}
body: After all that about {cause}, {who} and {other} have shaken hands. Neighbours report feeling slightly let down.

line: {who} carried {other} out of a fire, and that was the end of the feud.
head: {WHO} SAVES OLD ENEMY {OTHER}
body: They were not speaking. Then {who} went into the smoke and came out with {other} over one shoulder. Nobody has mentioned {cause} since.

line: With the wedding, the row over {cause} is over. {who} and {other} shook hands.
head: A WEDDING ENDS THE WAR
body: The families are one family now, so {who} and {other} have agreed that {cause} was nobody's fault. It was entirely somebody's fault.

line: {who} and {other} seem to have forgotten what the fuss about {cause} was.
head: THE GREAT ROW FIZZLES OUT
body: Nobody can quite remember why {who} and {other} fell out. It may have been {cause}.

line: A well-placed Hush has ended it. {who} and {other} are done arguing about {cause}.
head: HUSHED
body: The row over {cause} ended quite suddenly, in silence, with a faint smell of magic.

line: {who} took {other} out to say thank you for the rescue.
head: "THANK YOU" AT {PLACE}
body: {who} has bought {other} a meal at {place}, and promised to go on doing so for about a year.

line: The housewarming at {place}: {guests} guests, and everyone admired the new boards.
head: BACK IN, AND THE KETTLE'S ON
body: After the fire, the family at {place} had the street round. It still smells of new wood. Nobody minded.

line: {who} tidied up by magic and now nobody can find anything.
head: TIDY SPELL: EVERYTHING GONE
body: {who} cast a small Tidy in a bad mood. The house is spotless. The cutlery has not been seen since.

line: {who} tried a Warm and overdid it. There is a smell of toast, and it is the curtains.
head: WARM GOES HOT
body: A small Warm went further than planned when {who} cast it in a temper.

line: {who} tried to Mend the damage and made it worse. The repairs need more boards.
head: MENDED BACKWARDS
body: {who} cast a Mend on a burned wall and the wall has taken offence.

line: {who} tried to Hush {other}. {other} has never been louder.
head: HUSH BACKFIRES
body: The Hush that {who} cast on {other} did the opposite, and can be heard from the bridge.

line: {who} mended a burned room at {place} by magic.
head: ONE ROOM, GOOD AS NEW
body: {who} has saved the repair crew a day with one small Mend at {place}.

line: {who} Hushed {other}, and things have calmed down.
head: A QUIET WORD, LITERALLY
body: {who} cast a small Hush on {other}. Peace, for an hour or so.

line: {who} and {other} are going steady. Nobody is in a hurry.
head: {WHO} AND {OTHER}: NO RUSH
body: {who} and {other} have told this paper there are no plans, in a way that suggests there is a spreadsheet.

head: NOTHING HAPPENS IN ODDHAVEN
body: A quiet few days. We have checked twice.

column: This column has heard this much: {line}
Not that we are one to talk, but: {line}
part: Part {n} of a story this paper is following.
This paper has been following this one: part {n}.

pranks.note: left a very polite note, which is the worst kind
pranks.flyers: pinned up flyers asking if anyone had lost their manners
pranks.doorbell: taught the doorbell a new tune
pranks.cones: put traffic cones round the car, all of them
